purpose: Learn the supplied-entity reference contract, not clinical relation truth, label choice or direction.
chosen_policy: Keep the complete frozen positive completion byte-for-byte.
rejected_policy: Replace one endpoint name by an equal-completion-token-length, same-type donor name from another TRAIN group, absent from the full supplied entity table and original source/title. Leave all other fields and positive records unchanged.

limitations: These are entity-reference contract preferences, not a complete medical relation semantic discrimination solution.
Chosen retains the complete released row of silver annotations, not an exhaustive or clinically adjudicated relation graph.
No UNKNOWN pair was labelled negative; no direction or alternative in-table relation is asserted clinically false.
Mechanical holdout is split from frozen TRAIN groups; it is not a clinical or template-generalization evaluation.
Exact token-length equality removes total completion-length preference only; lexical, type, donor and source-absence shortcuts may remain.
Only short_source complete-overlap regular windows with at least two records are selected; scope is not all training rows.
One corrupted endpoint invalidates the whole rejected batch under the existing parser; all other original records remain byte-identical.

design_limitations: Disease/Symptom endpoint mutations only; long Diagnostic Criterion copying errors are outside this candidate set.
Source-group roles are disjoint but vocabulary/concept independence is not claimed.

All groups originate in frozen TRAIN, which prior SFT may already have seen. Mechanical holdout is only excluded from these preference-training candidates; it is not an unseen-base-model or clinical heldout set.
64 pairs cover only regular short_source windows with at least two positive annotation records; no representative population claim.
Completion token totals are exactly equal, but character counts differ (40 shorter rejected,22 longer,2 equal); lexical/name-frequency shortcuts remain possible.
Chosen silver annotations are retained, not newly clinically adjudicated.
This small candidate set is not evidence that DPO improves F1 or will solve all relation hallucination.
